title: Leveraging the Potential of Prompt Engineering for Hate Speech Detection in Low-Resource Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the performance (using F1 scores) of LLMs and deep learning baseline models on hate speech detection across low-resource languages (Bengali, Hindi) versus high-resource languages (English, German) to evaluate linguistic disparities.

Evaluating the LLM's excessive sensitivity and tendency to refuse processing prompts containing the word 'hate' due to built-in ethical guardrails, and testing 'metaphor prompting' (substituting 'hate' with words like 'red' or 'thorn') to bypass these restrictions.

Reversing the order of class definitions ('hate speech' versus 'not-hate speech') in zero-shot prompts to observe and measure the model's classification preference or bias towards predicting a specific class based on prompt framing.
